approach: Extend `check_environment_reach` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs with a CI cache-scope trigger and a completeness block. No new step! line, no new check, no change to `scan_segments`. Three lexical trigger forms, read only from behavior criteria and the summary. D1: a behavior-criterion segment has a cache/artifact word and a CI place. D2: a segment has a CI place, a reuse word, a result noun and a cross-ref word, and no sha/commit word (the er96 early-push shape; SHA-matched reuse is left alone). D3: a created or modified `.github/workflows/` deliverable exists and a behavior criterion or the summary has a cache/artifact word. `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact` are found by a small token test. When a trigger fires, the best `Environment:` assumption naming the cache, artifact or result must state noun, save, restore, write rights and scope; the error names what the best one lacks. Revision answers: (1) the existing test `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` (reading.rs:6947-6981) is edited to scope its negative 3% assertion to the defined-terms changelog item, and is added to dependents; (2) `workflow(s)` and `runner(s)` count as a CI place only beside `github` in the segment or when the reading has a non-delete `.github/workflows/` deliverable, with a 'the corpus runner caches the readings' accept control; (3) each of the four new INPUT_FORMS tags is mapped to a named corpus case.

decisions.choice: Extend check_environment_reach; add no new check or step! line.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading says to extend it. Cache save, restore and write scope is a fourth fact of the same Environment: statement. `refusing_check`, `environment_reach_has_one_step_line` (reading.rs:5178) and the acceptance doc list stay as they are, and the check is already in `acceptance_check_names`, so criterion 5 is met by the declaration test with share 3.

rejected.option: A new check_cache_scope with its own step!
rejected.why: It adds a step line and a second refusal-case requirement, and splits one Environment: statement across two checks with two error texts.

rejected.option: Add cache words to the site/permission/data lists
rejected.why: Those lists test one word each and cannot say which of save scope, restore scope or write rights is missing.

decisions.choice: Narrow trigger D2: CI place + reuse word (reuse, reuses, reused, reusing) + result noun (run, runs, pass, passes, result, results, status) + cross-ref word (early, earlier, push, pushes, pushed, pushing, branch, branches, land, lands, landing, another, previous, base, ref, refs) in one segment, and only when the segment has no sha, commit or commits word.
decisions.reason: Athena reuses a green CI run matched by commit SHA as an ordinary feature (routing.rs, verify.rs, records.rs); those are not branch-scoped caches. The er96 sentence 'an early push whose CI run is reused at landing' has early, push and landing, so it fires. 'a green CI result is reused as the job baseline when the fingerprint matches' (reading.rs:7445) has no cross-ref word and 'a green CI run for the candidate SHA is reused' names a SHA, so both stay accepted and become accept controls.

rejected.option: Keep D2 as CI place + reuse + result noun
rejected.why: It refuses ordinary routing and verification readings that say a CI result is reused.

rejected.option: Drop D2 and rely on cache words
rejected.why: The er96 wording has no cache word, so the class would be missed.

decisions.choice: Judge completeness on the Environment: assumptions that name a cache, artifact or result noun, reporting the missing parts of the best one (fewest missing of save, restore, write rights, scope). With no such assumption, name the missing noun and list all four parts. Never use the union.
decisions.reason: CI_ENVIRONMENT (reading.rs:4469) holds 'write' and 'refs'; a union would let a cache line without write rights pass or hide which part is missing. The assumption noun set is the cache words plus result, results, status, pass, passes (not 'run'), so CI_ENVIRONMENT is never a candidate. A pasted CI block that holds a write word still passes the write part; stated as a lexical limit.

rejected.why: It hides a missing write-rights or scope part when a CI block is also present.

decisions.choice: Build the bail! tail from the problems that fired. The old wording stays byte for byte when only the old block or the evidence block fired; a cache-only refusal says 'which ref saves the cache or artifact, which runs restore it and which runs may write shared entries'; both are joined with 'or'.
decisions.reason: The old tail describes the wrong problem for a cache-only refusal. Existing message tests (reading.rs:4840-4856) concern non-cache readings and are unchanged.

decisions.choice: Detect `actions/cache`, `actions/upload-artifact` and `actions/download-artifact` with a small token test (split on white space, backticks, commas, parentheses; trim punctuation; cut at '@'; lowercase). A match counts as both CI place and cache word, for behavior criteria and for the summary under D3.
decisions.reason: `scan_segments` splits at any token with '/' (surveys.rs:454), so 'actions/cache' is dropped there. A local test avoids changing segmentation for names_source and has_host_action.

rejected.why: It changes segmentation for every caller of scan_segments.

rejected.option: List it as a limit only
rejected.why: It is the usual way to name a GitHub cache, so the miss would be common.

decisions.choice: CI place (finding 2) = a word with `ci` set (CI written exactly), or `github` followed by `actions`, or workflow/workflows/runner/runners in a segment that also has a `github` word, or workflow/workflows/runner/runners anywhere when the reading has a non-delete `.github/workflows/` deliverable. Scope words are branch, branches, ref, refs, main, pr, prs, scope, scoped, plus 'default' only before branch, branches, ref or refs and 'pull' only before request or requests. Bare github, bare actions, lowercase ci and bare runner or workflow are not CI places.
decisions.reason: Athena's own wording uses 'runner' (the corpus runner) and 'workflow' generically, so a bare runner/workflow would trigger D1 on 'the corpus runner caches the readings'. Tying them to github or a real workflow deliverable removes that false positive; in a reading with a workflow deliverable D3 fires on a cache word anyway, so nothing is lost. 'by default' and 'main loop' would otherwise meet the scope part; 'main' is kept because the brief's example says 'written only by main'.

rejected.option: Count bare runner(s) and workflow(s) as a CI place
rejected.why: The critic's finding: 'the corpus runner caches the readings' would be refused with no CI cache involved.

rejected.option: Reuse ENV_SITE_WORDS as the CI list
rejected.why: It holds github, local, reader and producer, so a plain product cache would fire.

rejected.option: Accept bare default and pull as scope
rejected.why: A sentence could meet the scope part without naming a ref.

steps: In surveys.rs, after ENV_ABSENT_WORDS, add constants. ENV_CACHE_WORDS: cache, caches, cached, caching, artifact, artifacts. ENV_CI_PLACE_WORDS (weak places): workflow, workflows, runner, runners. ENV_REUSE_WORDS: reuse, reuses, reused, reusing. ENV_RESULT_WORDS (trigger side): run, runs, pass, passes, result, results, status. ENV_CROSS_REF_WORDS: early, earlier, push, pushes, pushed, pushing, branch, branches, land, lands, landing, another, previous, base, ref, refs. ENV_SAVE_WORDS: save, saves, saved, saving, store, stores, stored, upload, uploads, uploaded. ENV_RESTORE_WORDS: restore, restores, restored, restoring, download, downloads, downloaded, reuse, reuses, reused, reusing. ENV_WRITE_RIGHTS_WORDS: write, writes, written, writable, readonly, permission, permissions (plain `read` excluded). ENV_SCOPE_WORDS: branch, branches, ref, refs, main, pr, prs, scope, scoped. Also an assumption-side noun list: the cache words plus result, results, status, pass, passes (not `run`).

In surveys.rs, add `segment_has_cache_scope_trigger(seg: &[EnvWord], has_workflow_deliverable: bool) -> bool` next to segment_has_host_action. A CI place is a word with `ci` set, `github` followed by `actions`, a weak place word (workflow(s), runner(s)) in a segment that also has a `github` word, or a weak place word when has_workflow_deliverable is true. It returns true for D1 (CI place and a cache word), or for D2 (CI place, a reuse word, a result word and a cross-ref word, and no `sha`, `commit` or `commits` word). Add `names_actions_cache(text: &str) -> bool`: split on white space, backticks, commas and parentheses, trim punctuation, cut at `@`, compare in lowercase with actions/cache, actions/upload-artifact and actions/download-artifact. Add a scope test over plain_words that takes `default` only before branch, branches, ref or refs and `pull` only before request or requests. Do not change scan_segments.

In check_environment_reach compute `cache_trigger`: D1/D2 on any behavior-criterion segment, or `names_actions_cache` on a behavior criterion, or (D3) a non-delete `.github/workflows/` deliverable exists and a behavior criterion or the summary has a cache word in a scanned segment (or names actions/cache). Add `&& !cache_trigger` to the early return. After the old block and before the evidence block, when cache_trigger holds, push a trigger text naming CI caches, stored artifacts and reused CI results. Candidates are the Environment: assumptions whose plain_words hold a noun from the assumption-side list. An assumption is complete if it holds a save, restore, write-rights and scope word. If none is complete, take the candidate with the fewest missing parts and push a problem naming each missing part ('which ref and event saves it', 'which runs restore it', 'which runs may write shared entries', 'the ref scope'). If there are no candidates, name the missing 'cache, artifact or result' and list all four parts as to be stated in one assumption. Quote the brief's example sentence in the repair text.

In check_environment_reach build the bail! tail from the problems that fired: the old tail wording unchanged when the old block or the evidence block fired, the cache tail ('which ref saves the cache or artifact, which runs restore it and which runs may write shared entries') when the cache block fired, joined with 'or' when both did. Edit the doc comment: reword 'It reads four things and nothing else' to list the added input. Add a paragraph with the root cause 'no step asking, for each CI cache or stored artifact, which ref saves it, which runs restore it, and which runs may write shared entries', jobs 20261025-034731-2am0 and 20261025-055626-er96, introspections 20261025-050603-wrv7 and 20261025-065849-n99a. State the limits (lexical; lowercase `ci` missed; SHA-matched reuse of CI results deliberately not a trigger; bare runner or workflow not a CI place; a pasted CI block can meet the write and scope words) and end with: 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended, expected 3% of newly refused readings (an estimate, not measured).' Leave the old paragraphs and their 8% sentence untouched.

In reading.rs tests, after `environment_reach_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause`, add: `environment_reach_cache_refuses_a_workflow_with_a_cache_without_scope`, `environment_reach_cache_refuses_a_behavior_cache_criterion_without_scope` (including the actions/cache form, the CI-block-plus-cache-sentence-without-write-rights case and the cache-only tail assertion), `environment_reach_cache_scope_covers_the_class` (both job shapes plus all controls, including 'the corpus runner caches the readings', the baseline sentence and the SHA routing sentence), `environment_reach_cache_scope_accepts_the_criteria_and_summary_of_its_own_job` and `environment_reach_cache_scope_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` (finds the new item by the new cause string). Fixtures put the cache word in a behavior criterion.

In reading.rs, edit `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` (6947-6981). Build the changelog items as `environment_reach_doc_and_changelog_name_the_cause` does (reading.rs:5225-5241: split at '## [Unreleased]', join continuation lines, collapse white space). Find the item that contains both '`reading::check_defined_terms`' and 'expected 2% of newly refused readings'. Run the 2% positive and 3% negative assertions on that item for the changelog (the doc comment keeps them as now). Keep the needle loop on the whole collapsed changelog and every D164 assertion. Add a comment saying the scope narrowed because check_environment_reach now declares 3% in the same Unreleased section.

In refusal_corpus.rs, add `ci-cache-criterion`, `ci-result-reuse-criterion`, `cache-scope-assumption` and `cache-word-in-product-or-path` to INPUT_FORMS and change `[&str; 41]` to `[&str; 45]`. Add the thirteen cases listed in demonstration 5 to environment_cases() (five refuse, eight accept, including environment-corpus-runner-cache-accepted) with the tag-to-case map given there, sources naming jobs 20261025-034731-2am0 and 20261025-055626-er96, 'rebuilt from the job brief'. Add `environment_cache_scope_refusal_is_declared_intended` (name present in acceptance_check_names, replay_declaration gives Some(3), doc comment and CHANGELOG needles).

In CHANGELOG.md add an Unreleased Added item at the top. It names the cause (no step asking, for each CI cache or stored artifact, which ref saves it, which runs restore it, and which runs may write shared entries), the extension of `check_environment_reach`, the required `Environment:` assumption stating save scope, restore scope and write rights, the test names, the follow-up to add the cache clause to the reader rule line in briefs.rs within 220 bytes, and 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended, expected 3% of newly refused readings.' Do not include the old CAUSE sentence and do not touch the defined-terms item (lines 114-140), whose 2% wording the edited test finds.

Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo test -p athena-core, cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings and cargo test --locked. Fix fixture wording until all pass; do not weaken the check to make a fixture pass.

risks.risk: False positives push the refusal share above 3%: a CI place plus a cache word with no CI cache involved, or a reused CI result that is not a ref-scoped stored result.
risks.mitigation: CI place needs `CI` written exactly, GitHub Actions, workflow(s) or runner(s) beside github or with a real workflow deliverable, or an actions/* cache name. D2 needs a cross-ref word and excludes sha and commit. scan_segments drops paths, identifiers and non-command backticks. Accept controls cover the in-process cache, a path, the GitHub API response cache, 'CI runs the tests', 'the corpus runner caches the readings', the baseline sentence and the SHA routing sentence. The replay at verification measures the real share; 3% is labelled an estimate not measured, because records are absent from the snapshot.

risks.risk: D2 still fires on text such as 'the CI run is reused after the push' that is SHA-matched in fact.
risks.mitigation: The doc comment states the limit; the error tells the reader what to write, so the cost is one retry. The sha/commit exclusion covers wording that names the matching key.

Adjust fixture wording, not the check.

risks.mitigation: State it as a lexical limit in the doc comment, as the existing check does. The save and restore parts are still required in the same assumption, and the repair text quotes the brief's example.

risks.risk: The new doc paragraph or CHANGELOG item breaks tests that read them: the old environment doc/changelog tests (CAUSE string, 8%) and `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` (negative 3% on the whole changelog).

risks.mitigation: The error text states what to write and quotes an example. The CHANGELOG item names the follow-up and open_questions asks the user to decide.
